chapters.screenText: Start here in CryoLauncher. Choose Cloud for this tutorial.

chapters.title: Start here
instructions: Open CryoLauncher and sign in. Use an approved connected cloud account with its resources prepared.
The following steps select this tutorial’s model and example.
chapters.note: Shared application orientation; the case-specific configuration follows.
chapters.why: Your workspace keeps scripts, dataset references and results together.

chapters.screenText: Choose Cloud → Advanced → Icepack → Tutorial / 02 Synthetic Ice Shelf.
chapters.screenWhy: Choose the intended interface, model and example before editing or launching a run.
chapters.expectedResult: Use an owned workspace clone before replacing source.
chapters.title: 1. Choose the Advanced shelf example
instructions: Choose Cloud → Advanced → Icepack → Tutorial / 02 Synthetic Ice Shelf.
Create an owned workspace copy before replacing source.
chapters.note: The application example remains read-only.
chapters.why: Choose the intended interface, model and example before editing or launching a run.

chapters.screenText: Enter a new name and choose Clone to My Workspace.
chapters.screenWhy: Cloning gives you an editable copy while preserving the supplied application source.
chapters.expectedResult: The canonical application source stays read-only.
chapters.title: 2. Clone to your workspace
instructions: Enter a new name, then choose Clone to My Workspace.
chapters.note: This example is named pilot-icepack-advanced-1118.
chapters.why: Cloning gives you an editable copy while preserving the supplied application source.

chapters.screenText: Wait for the cloned-workspace confirmation and saved file status.
chapters.screenWhy: Cloning gives you an editable copy while preserving the supplied application source.
chapters.expectedResult: This owned example is pilot-icepack-advanced-1118.
chapters.title: 2. Confirm the editable clone
instructions: Wait for Cloned to your workspace.
The file selector contains run.py and the status changes to saved.
chapters.note: You will replace run.py only inside this owned clone.
chapters.why: Cloning gives you an editable copy while preserving the supplied application source.

chapters.screenText: Choose the one-change run.py in your file picker; Open.
chapters.screenWhy: Selecting local files prepares them for import; importing saves them in this example.
chapters.expectedResult: Check that one script file is selected.
chapters.title: 3. Choose your replacement run.py
instructions: Choose script files. In your file picker select the one-change run.py, then choose Open.
chapters.note: Check that the picker shows one selected file.
chapters.why: Selecting local files prepares them for import; importing saves them in this example.

chapters.screenText: Check the selected script before replacing the existing file.
chapters.screenWhy: Selecting local files prepares them for import; importing saves them in this example.
chapters.expectedResult: Retain both 400-year phases and 200 steps per phase: dt = 2 years.
chapters.title: 3. Check the selected file
instructions: One script file is selected.
The replacement must keep the original source except for 255.15 → 254.15 K.
chapters.note: Both 400-year phases retain 200 steps each, at 2 years per step.
chapters.why: Selecting local files prepares them for import; importing saves them in this example.

chapters.screenText: Enable Replace existing script files.
chapters.screenWhy: Replacement explicitly allows an imported file to overwrite the same name in this clone.
chapters.expectedResult: Your clone already contains run.py.
chapters.title: 4. Enable intentional replacement
instructions: Enable Replace existing script files.
Your clone already contains run.py, so replacing it requires this checkbox.
chapters.note: Keep the temperature edit in your local replacement file.
chapters.why: Replacement explicitly allows an imported file to overwrite the same name in this clone.

chapters.screenText: Choose Import script files.
chapters.screenWhy: Import saves the selected source files in this example; it does not launch the model.
chapters.expectedResult: Importing saves the replacement; it does not launch a model.
chapters.title: 4. Import and save the new source
instructions: Choose Import script files.
chapters.note: Importing saves files; it does not launch a model.
chapters.why: Import saves the selected source files in this example; it does not launch the model.

chapters.screenText: Wait for Imported run.py. Files are saved.
chapters.screenWhy: Import saves the selected source files in this example; it does not launch the model.
chapters.expectedResult: Keep run.py as the Run target.
chapters.title: 4. Confirm the saved source
instructions: Wait for Imported run.py. Files are saved.
Keep run.py as the Run target.
chapters.note: The submitted source was verified to contain this temperature-only change.
chapters.why: Import saves the selected source files in this example; it does not launch the model.

chapters.screenText: Check cloud readiness and retain 2 vCPU / 8 GiB.
chapters.screenWhy: Ready indicates that the required account resources are configured for the run.
chapters.expectedResult: Review the owned clone and run.py target.
chapters.title: 5. Review the cloud configuration
instructions: Confirm Account connected and Storage, Containers and Compute Ready.
Choose Review & Launch and check the owned clone and run.py.
chapters.note: Retain 2 vCPU and 8 GiB for this native run.
chapters.why: Ready indicates that the required account resources are configured for the run.

chapters.screenText: Choose Review & Launch.
chapters.screenWhy: Review confirms the intended model, source, resources and charges before submission.
chapters.expectedResult: The displayed runtime is an estimate, not measured model duration.
chapters.title: 5. Open the review
instructions: Choose Review & Launch.
chapters.note: The displayed ~60 minutes is an estimate, not a measured model duration.
chapters.why: Review confirms the intended model, source, resources and charges before submission.

chapters.screenText: Control guide: confirm Launch cloud run when checks are Ready.
chapters.screenWhy: This confirmation stages the reviewed inputs and starts a paid cloud job.
chapters.expectedResult: The following card belongs to this tutorial’s original native run.
chapters.title: 5. Confirm the launch
instructions: Choose Launch cloud run when the readiness checks are ready.
This confirmation starts the run.
chapters.note: Control guide; the following card belongs to this tutorial’s original native run.
chapters.why: This confirmation stages the reviewed inputs and starts a paid cloud job.

chapters.screenText: Follow the new Advanced clone run card.
chapters.screenWhy: Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.
chapters.expectedResult: Wait for completion, then open View results.
chapters.title: 5. Follow the new submission
instructions: The new run card names pilot-icepack-advanced-1118.
Allow the job to finish, then open View results.
chapters.note: Importing the replacement file did not submit it automatically.
chapters.why: Submission, queue/startup and native model execution are separate stages.

chapters.screenText: Select icepack → velocity in Results; Render when needed.

chapters.note: The first field may be previewed automatically.

instructions: Read the field name and units before interpreting the map.

instructions: Colour is speed in m/year; arrows show direction. The x and y axes are metres.
